audits.title: P081 Out-patient management of gout in secondary care: Results from the North West regional audit
audits.standard: NICE, EULAR, BSR and MHRA gout guidelines
audits.setting: 13 rheumatology outpatient departments in Greater Manchester and Lancashire (North West regional audit)

cycle1.result: Treat-to-target levels agreed in 49 (57%); cardiovascular risk tool used in 3 (3%); no patient with major cardiovascular disease on febuxostat; 16 (17%) no planned follow-up; 18 (78%) new patients appropriately referred; 15 (75%) started on first-line ULT; 11 (79%) allopurinol started at low dose; 10 (67%) given colchicine prophylaxis.

audits.other_findings: None of 12 patients with hypertension without heart failure on diuretics received advice to reduce or stop them. Clinic data would have allowed cardiovascular risk calculation in 13 (14%).
audits.citation: Gould L, Richards A, Gray L, Badarulla M, Mercer L, Farid R, et al.. P081 Out-patient management of gout in secondary care: Results from the North West regional audit. Rheumatology. 2024;63(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.122.

audits.title: An audit of the variability of diagnosis and management of gout in the rheumatology setting: the gout evaluation and management study.
audits.standard: EULAR recommendations for gout diagnosis and management

cycle1.result: Diagnostic recommendations adherence 26.0% (crystal-proven diagnosis 26%); comorbidity evaluation 50.6%; acute flare management 100%; lifestyle 71.4%; urate-lowering therapy 52.1%.

audits.citation: Perez-Ruiz F, Carmona L, Yébenes MJ, Pascual E, de Miguel E, Ureña I, et al.. An audit of the variability of diagnosis and management of gout in the rheumatology setting: the gout evaluation and management study. J Clin Rheumatol. 2011;17(7):349-355. doi:10.1097/rhu.0b013e3182314d40. PMID: 21946457.

audits.title: Improvement in the management of gout is vital and overdue: an audit from a UK primary care medical practice.
audits.standard: Criteria from EULAR and BSR/BHPR gout guidelines; standards set locally
audits.setting: One primary care medical practice, North Staffordshire

cycle1.result: 74% (226) had serum uric acid recorded, 11% (34) eGFR ever, 53% (162) glucose; 34% (105) ever and 25% (77) currently on urate-lowering therapy.

audits.other_findings: Dose titration to serum uric acid, lifestyle advice and comorbidity consideration were inadequate.
audits.citation: Cottrell E, Crabtree V, Edwards JJ, Roddy E. Improvement in the management of gout is vital and overdue: an audit from a UK primary care medical practice. BMC Fam Pract. 2013;14:170. doi:10.1186/1471-2296-14-170. PMID: 24225170.

audits.title: Inpatient management of gout in a New Zealand hospital: a retrospective audit.
audits.standard: Published gout protocols including treat-to-target urate management

cycle1.result: 50% of known gout patients on urate-lowering therapy; serum urate measured in 60%; treat-to-target mentioned in only 9%.

audits.other_findings: Rheumatology review associated with more polytherapy, intra-articular steroids, ACTH and allopurinol.
audits.citation: Kennedy NJ, Healy PJ, Harrison AA. Inpatient management of gout in a New Zealand hospital: a retrospective audit. Int J Rheum Dis. 2016;19(2):205-210. doi:10.1111/1756-185x.12578. PMID: 25873399.

audits.title: Improving management of gout in primary care using a customised electronic records template.
audits.standard: Current gout guidance: serum uric acid (SUA) checked in past 12 months, SUA below target, lifestyle advice in past 12 months; audit standard 60% at 2 months and 80% at 4 months

cycle1.result: 51 (40%) had SUA checked in past 12 months; 88 (25%) had SUA below target; lifestyle advice not recorded.

audits.intervention: Custom electronic EMIS template displaying gout guidance and allowing data entry, with education of GPs and administrative staff.

cycle2.result: 112 (84%) had SUA checked; 79 (51%) had SUA below target; 76 (57%) received lifestyle advice.

audits.other_findings: Standard not reached for two of the three criteria.
audits.citation: Moffat K, McNab D. Improving management of gout in primary care using a customised electronic records template. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u204832.w2038. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u204832.w2038. PMID: 26734335.

audits.title: Management of gout by UK rheumatologists: a British Society for Rheumatology national audit.
audits.standard: Audit standards from 2006 EULAR recommendations, 2007 BSR/BHPR gout guideline and NICE febuxostat technology appraisal
audits.setting: 91 UK rheumatology outpatient departments (BSR national audit)

cycle1.result: Diagnosis crystal-proven in 13%; diuretic reduced/stopped in 29% of 106; ULT continued/initiated in 76% of those with an indication; allopurinol started at 100 mg daily in 82% of 158; fewer than half reached target serum uric acid at 12 months.

audits.citation: Roddy E, Packham J, Obrenovic K, Rivett A, Ledingham JM. Management of gout by UK rheumatologists: a British Society for Rheumatology national audit. Rheumatology (Oxford). 2018;57(5):826-830. doi:10.1093/rheumatology/kex521. PMID: 29447370.
